title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Effects of vitamins C and E supplementation combined with 12-week resistance training in older women with sarcopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Xu Liu, Bo Chen, Yutian Jin, Feiyan Zhong, Yunjuan Zhang, Yu Li, Yun Zhang, Runhong Cui, Bing Wu, Cu...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C, E, and resistance training in older women with sarcopenia. Supplementation with vitamins C and E enhanced muscle mass and strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: Vitamin D 3  supplementation does not enhance the effects of resistance training in older adults
authors: Knut Sindre Mølmen, Daniel Hammarström, Karianne Pedersen, Anne Cecilie Lian Lie, Ragnvald B. Steile...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation on resistance training outcomes in older adults. Vitamin D3 supplementation did not enhance improvements in muscle strength, mass, or endurance compared to placebo.

title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: The effect of combined resistance exercise training and vitamin D 3  supplementation on musculoskeletal health and function in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Antoniak, Carolyn A Greig
abstract: This systematic review evaluated combined resistance exercise and vitamin D supplementation in older adults. The combination significantly improved lower limb muscle strength compared to exercise alone.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Effect of vitamin E succinate on inflammatory cytokines induced by high-intensity interval training
authors: Hadi Sarir, Ghodsieh Emdadifard, Homayoun Farhangfar, Hossein TaheriChadorneshin
source: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences : The Official Journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E succinate's effect on inflammatory cytokines after high-intensity interval training in rats. Vitamin E succinate supplementation reduced HIIT-induced increases in IL-6 and TNF-α.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: The effect of endurance training with and without vitamin E on expression of p53 and PTEN tumor suppressing genes in prostate glands of male rats
authors: Amin Allah Dashtiyan, Masood Sepehrimanesh, Nader Tanideh, Mohammad Esmaeil Afzalpour
abstract: Endurance training was studied for its effect on prostate tumor suppressor genes in rats, with and without vitamin E. Endurance training reduced p53 expression, while vitamin E alone increased PTEN expression.

title: Elastic resistance training is more effective than vitamin D3 supplementation in reducing oxidative stress and strengthen antioxidant enzymes in healthy men
authors: Fardin Kalvandi, Mohammad Ali Azarbayjani, Ronak Azizbeigi, Kamal Azizbeigi
abstract: Elastic resistance training was studied with and without vitamin D3 supplementation in healthy men. Elastic resistance training alone was more effective than with vitamin D3 supplementation for reducing oxidative stress and strengthening antioxidant enzymes.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation and high intensity interval training induced changes in lipid profile and haematological variables of young males
authors: Surojit Sarkar, Swapan Kr Dey, Gouriprosad Datta, Amit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in young males. Supplementation protected against negative hematological changes and improved lipid profiles and explosive strength without affecting endurance.

title: Effects of Resistance Training Combined with Vitamin D Supplementation on Health-Related Variables in the Elderly: Muscle Strength, Body Composition, and Inflammatory Status
authors: Lorena Cristina Ribeiro da Rosa, Paulo de Tarso Veras Farinatti, Maria Izabel Ferreira Batista, Hile...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study examined the effects of resistance training plus vitamin D supplementation on older adults. The combination did not improve strength, body composition, or inflammation more than resistance training alone.

title: Effects of Vitamin D3 Supplementation and Resistance Training on 25-Hydroxyvitamin D Status and Functional Performance of Older Adults: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Rudolf Aschauer, Sandra Unterberger, Patrick A. Zöhrer, Agnes Draxler, Bernhard Franzke, Eva-Maria S...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation and resistance training on older adults. Vitamin D supplementation improved vitamin D status but did not enhance muscle performance or functional mobility beyond resistance training alone.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on renal non-enzymatic antioxidants in young rats submitted to exhaustive exercise stress
authors: Sérvio A Bucioli, Luiz Carlos de Abreu, Vitor E Valenti, Claudio Leone, Helio Vannucchi
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effects on renal antioxidants in young rats undergoing exhaustive exercise. Vitamin E supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and increased antioxidant levels in the kidneys.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Has No Impact on Cardiorespiratory Fitness, but Improves Inflammatory Status in Vitamin D Deficient Young Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Luule Medijainen, Lisette Tõnutare, Frederik Ross, ...
abstract: Vitamin D supplementation was studied in deficient young men undergoing resistance training. It improved inflammatory status but did not affect cardiorespiratory fitness.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Supplementation with α-Lipoic Acid, CoQ10, and Vitamin E Augments Running Performance and Mitochondrial Function in Female Mice
authors: Arkan Abadi, Justin D. Crane, Daniel Ogborn, Bart Hettinga, Mahmood Akhtar, Andrew Stokl, Lauren Mac...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an antioxidant cocktail on running performance and mitochondrial function in mice. The supplement improved performance and mitochondrial function in untrained female mice, but not in trained mice.

title: Effect of vitamin e supplementation with exercise on cognitive functions and total antioxidant capacity in older people
authors: E. Çetin; E.C. Top; G. Şahin; Y. Gül. Özkaya; H. Aydin; F. Toraman
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: We investigated the effects of six months vitamin E administration on cognition evaluated by event-related potentials in exercising older subjects. Randomised controlled trial. Retirement home in Anta

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation and circuit training on indices of obesity and insulin resistance in T2D and vitamin D deficient elderly women
authors: Hyoung-Jun Kim, Chang-Kyun Kang, Hyon Park, Man-Gyoon Lee
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamin D and circuit training on obese, vitamin D-deficient elderly women with type 2 diabetes. Circuit training alone improved body composition, abdominal fat, and blood lipids, while combined treatment showed a trend toward improved insulin resistance.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation Delays Cellular Senescence  In Vitro
authors: Giorgio La Fata, Nicole Seifert, Peter Weber, M. Hasan Mohajeri
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on cellular senescence in human cells. Vitamin E supplementation reduced senescent cells by downregulating P21 expression.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: A metabolomic investigation of the effects of vitamin E supplementation in humans
authors: Max Wong, John K Lodge
abstract: This study investigated plasma metabolome changes after vitamin E supplementation in healthy males. Vitamin E supplementation altered lysophosphatidylcholine levels, suggesting an influence on phospholipid metabolism.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Antioxidant Effects and Insulin Resistance Improvement of Chromium Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Ming-Hoang Lai
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of chromium, vitamin C, and E supplementation on type 2 diabetes patients. Combined supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress and improved glucose metabolism.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Does Not Enhance Gains in Muscle Strength and Lean Body Mass or Influence Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Vitamin D-Insufficient Middle-Aged Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Evelin Mäestu, Luule Medijainen, Märt Lellsaar, Kri...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D supplementation's effect on resistance training outcomes in vitamin D-insufficient men. Vitamin D supplementation did not enhance muscle strength, lean body mass, or cardiorespiratory fitness gains.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Modification of the Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on the Mortality of Male Smokers by Age and Dietary Vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: Vitamin E supplementation's effect on mortality in male smokers was examined. Its impact varied significantly by age and dietary vitamin C intake, suggesting heterogeneous effects in different population subgroups.

title: Tissue-Specific Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Eugene Jansen, Dale Viezeliene, Piet Beekhof, Eric Gremmer, Leonid Ivanov
abstract: A study supplemented mice with varying vitamin E doses, including a high dose (25× RDI). High vitamin E intake showed beneficial effects in male mouse livers but caused toxicity and inflammation in male mouse kidneys.

title: Prevention of Mammary Tumorigenesis in Acatalasemic Mice by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Kunihiko Ishii, Li‐Xue Zhen, Da‐hong Wang, Yuka Funamori, Katsuo Ogawa, Kazuhisa Taketa
source: Japanese Journal of Cancer Research : Gann
abstract: Acatalasemic mice were studied to assess vitamin E's effect on mammary tumors. Vitamin E supplementation significantly reduced mammary tumor incidence in these mice.

title: Astaxanthin-, β-Carotene-, and Resveratrol-Rich Foods Support Resistance Training-Induced Adaptation
authors: Aki Kawamura, Wataru Aoi, Ryo Abe, Yukiko Kobayashi, Masashi Kuwahata, Akane Higashi
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with nutrient-rich foods on muscle adaptation in men. Consuming foods rich in astaxanthin, β-carotene, and resveratrol enhanced strength and metabolic improvements from training.

title: Vitamin E in Sarcopenia: Current Evidences on Its Role in Prevention and Treatment
authors: Shy Cian Khor, Norwahidah Abdul Karim, Wan Zurinah Wan Ngah, Yasmin Anum Mohd Yusof, Suzana Makpol
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's potential role in preventing and treating sarcopenia, an age-related muscle loss syndrome. While promising antioxidant properties exist, current evidence for its direct impact on muscle health remains inconclusive.

title: Effect of resistance training with and without vitamin D calcium chitosan nanoparticle supplements on apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats: An experimental study
authors: Mahsa Dehghan-Manshadi, Mohammad-Ali Azarbayjani, Sirvan Atashak, Maghsoud Peeri, Saleh Rahmati-Ahma...
abstract: This study examined how resistance training and vitamin D/calcium/chitosan nanoparticles affect apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats. The combination of resistance training and supplements appeared to reverse OVX-induced apoptosis.

title: The association of oxidative stress of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and vitamin E supplementation
authors: Mohamed Zaeim Hafez Ahmed, Reham Helmy Amin Helmy Saad, Ahmad Gadalla, Ramadan Hassan Ibrahim Thabet...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin E supplementation on neonatal hyperbilirubinemia treated with phototherapy. Vitamin E significantly reduced serum bilirubin levels and the duration of phototherapy.

title: Can Low-Dose of Dietary Vitamin E Supplementation Reduce Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress? A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Myunghee Kim, Hyeyoon Eo, Josephine Gahyun Lim, Hyunjung Lim, Yunsook Lim
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effects of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage. Low-dose vitamin E, especially under 500 IU, was found to reduce muscle damage, particularly in athletes.

title: Vitamin E (α-tocopherol) supplementation in diabetic rats: effects on the proximal colon
authors: Luciana P Roldi, Renata VF Pereira, Eleandro A Tronchini, Gabriela V Rizo, Célia R Scoaris, Jacqueli...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation on the proximal colons of diabetic rats. Vitamin E (2%) reduced blood sugar and protected myenteric neurons, but did not alter intestinal wall structure.

title: Effect of vitamin E supplementation on chicken sperm quality: A meta-analysis
authors: Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, Anuraga Jayanegara, Mohammad Miftakhus Sholikin, Supardi Rusdiana...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of dietary vitamin E on rooster sperm quality. Vitamin E supplementation significantly improved sperm concentration, motility, viability, and fertility, while reducing sperm death.

title: Low-Frequency Fatigue as an Indicator of Eccentric Exercise-Induced Muscle Injury: The Role of Vitamin E
authors: Antonios Kyparos, Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Konstantina Dipla, Andreas Zafeiridis, Vassilis Paschalis,...
abstract: This study examined if vitamin E reduces eccentric exercise-induced muscle injury in rats, using low-frequency fatigue as an indicator. Vitamin E supplementation improved muscle force decline and recovery, suggesting it attenuates exercise-induced injury.

title: Complex Effects of Vitamin E and Vitamin C Supplementation on  in Vitro  Neonatal Mononuclear Cell Responses to Allergens
authors: Heather J. H. Wassall, Graham Devereux, Anthony Seaton, Robert N. Barker
abstract: This study examined how vitamin E and C supplementation affects neonatal immune cells' response to allergens. Vitamin E showed complex effects, sometimes reducing proliferation and other times increasing it, while vitamin C had varied impacts on cytokine production.

title: Effects of 12-weeks resistance training and vitamin E supplementation on aminotransferases, CTRP-2, and CTRP-9 levels in males with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: a double-blind, randomized trial
authors: Irfan Varmazyar, Amir Abbas Monazzami, Mozhgan Moradi, Andrew J McAinch
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: Resistance training and vitamin E supplementation were studied in males with NAFLD. Resistance training improved health markers, with vitamin E adding benefits only for aminotransferase levels.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on sow gestation: a meta-analysis
authors: Ni Wayan Helpina Widyasanti, Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, I. Putu Cahyadi Putra, Jonathan Anug...
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated vitamin E supplementation in pregnant sows. Vitamin E significantly increased serum α-tocopherol in sows and piglets, but did not affect litter size or weight.

title: Effects of low-volume walking programme and vitamin E supplementation on oxidative damage and health-related variables in healthy older adults
authors: Jong-Hwan Park, Masashi Miyashita, Masaki Takahashi, Noriaki Kawanishi, Seong-Ryu Bae, Hyun-Shik Kim...
abstract: A low-volume walking program and vitamin E supplementation were studied in older adults. Both interventions, individually or combined, reduced oxidative damage markers.

title: The interaction effects of aerobic exercise training and vitamin D supplementation on plasma lipid profiles and insulin resistance in ovariectomized rats
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Rastegar Hoseini
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of aerobic exercise and vitamin D on ovariectomized rats. The combination significantly improved lipid profiles and reduced insulin resistance.

title: Vitamin C, A and E supplementation decreases the expression of  HSPA1A  and  HSPB1  genes in the leukocytes of young polish figure skaters during a 10-day training camp
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Zbigniew Jastrzębski, Grzegorz Chruściński, Monika Michałowska–Sawczyn, Alicja...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin A, C, and E supplementation on gene expression in young figure skaters during a training camp. Supplementation significantly decreased the expression of stress-related genes HSPA1A and HSPB1 in leukocytes.

title: Combined effect of high-dose vitamin A, vitamin E supplementation, and zinc on adult patients with diabetes: A randomized trial
authors: Eman Said, Shrook Mousa, May Fawzi, Nirmeen A. Sabry, Samar Farid
abstract: This randomized trial investigated the effects of vitamin A plus E supplementation, with and without zinc, on adult patients with type 2 diabetes. The combination of vitamins A and E with zinc significantly improved glycemic control and insulin secretion compared to a control group.

title: Aging Brain: Prevention of Oxidative Stress by Vitamin E and Exercise
authors: Sambe Asha Devi
abstract: This study investigated how vitamin E and exercise affect the aging brain's cognitive decline. Findings suggest these interventions can slow decline by reducing oxidative stress and potentially acting synergistically.

title: Various Effects of Omega 3 and Omega 3 Plus Vitamin E Supplementations on Serum Glucose Level and Insulin Resistance in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease
authors: Somayeh SABOORI, Mahmoud DJALALI, Esmaeil YOUSEFI RAD, Ebrahim Nematipour, Ali Akbar SABOOR-YARAGHI,...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of omega 3 and vitamin E supplementation on glucose and insulin levels in coronary artery disease patients. Co-administering omega 3 and vitamin E beneficially decreased insulin and insulin resistance, while omega 3 alone increased glucose.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Excessive Vitamin E Supplementation: Implications for Ovarian Physiology and Reproductive Health
authors: Farzaneh Rabiee, Masoud Fattahi, Mohammad Iranzad, Mohsen Rahimi Andani, Farnoosh Jafarpour, Mohamma...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different vitamin E doses on mouse reproductive health. Excessive vitamin E supplementation impaired fertility, oocyte and embryo development, and ovarian function by altering oxidative stress markers.

title: Resistance-Trained Individuals Are Less Susceptible to Oxidative Damage after Eccentric Exercise
authors: Ypatios Spanidis, Dimitrios Stagos, Christina Papanikolaou, Konstantina Karatza, Andria Theodosi, Ar...
abstract: Resistance-trained individuals experienced less oxidative damage and had a stronger antioxidant profile after eccentric exercise compared to untrained individuals. This suggests training status significantly influences exercise-induced oxidative stress and recovery.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation combined with resistance exercise on body composition and metabolic variables in older women: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Illana Patricia da Silva Queiroz; Angélica Castilho Alonso; Vanderlei Carneiro da Silva; Adriana Mac...
abstract: This trial investigated vitamin D and resistance exercise in older women. The combination improved body composition and metabolic variables, suggesting a synergistic effect for muscle and bone health.

title: Resistance training might have improved insulin resistance by attenuating sarcopenia
authors: Yildiray Topcu, Fatih Tufan, M Akif Karan

title: Muscle-Related Effect of Whey Protein and Vitamin D 3  Supplementation Provided before or after Bedtime in Males Undergoing Resistance Training
authors: Yan Chen, Yiheng Liang, Hang Guo, Kun Meng, Junqiang Qiu, Dan Benardot
abstract: This study examined the effects of whey protein and vitamin D supplementation before or after sleep on muscle mass and strength during resistance training. Both supplementation timings led to significant improvements in muscle mass and hormones compared to a placebo.

title: Effect of Vitamins A, C, and E Supplementation in the Treatment of Metabolic Syndrome in Albino Rats
authors: L. S. Bilbis, S. A. Muhammad, Y. Saidu, Y. Adamu
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamins A, C, and E on metabolic syndrome in rats fed a high-salt diet. Vitamin supplementation significantly reduced blood pressure, improved lipid profiles, and increased antioxidant status, suggesting a protective role.

title: A blinded, placebo‐controlled study on the clinical effects of vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis
authors: Casey L. Gordon, Samantha J. Reeves, Richard K. Burchell, Craig Thomson, Arnon Gal, Nicolas Lopez‐Vi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis. Vitamin E did not improve pain, lameness, quality of life, or reduce pain medication needs.

title: A Vitamin E-Enriched Antioxidant Diet Interferes with the Acute Adaptation of the Liver to Physical Exercise in Mice
authors: Miriam Hoene, Martin Irmler, Johannes Beckers, Martin Hrabě de Angelis, Hans-Ulrich Häring, Cora Wei...
abstract: A study examined how a vitamin E-enriched diet affects the liver's response to exercise in mice. High vitamin E intake disrupted the liver's normal metabolic and inflammatory adaptations to physical activity.

title: Influence of Vitamin E Supplementation on Glycaemic Control: A Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials
authors: Renfan Xu, Shasha Zhang, Anyu Tao, Guangzhi Chen, Muxun Zhang
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E supplementation's effect on glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes. Vitamin E supplementation did not significantly improve HbA1c, fasting glucose, or fasting insulin, except in patients with low baseline vitamin E.

title: The effect of Vitamin E supplementation on treatment of chronic periodontitis
authors: Parichehr Behfarnia, Mina Dadmehr, Seyedeh Negin Hosseini, Seyed Amir Mirghaderi
abstract: This study investigated Vitamin E supplementation's effect on chronic periodontitis treatment. Vitamin E significantly reduced attachment loss compared to standard treatment alone.

title: Resistance-based training improves mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in aging adults, independent of polyphenol supplementation
authors: Mathias Flensted-Jensen, Cecilie Moe Weinreich, Ann-Sofie Kleis-Olsen, Filip Hansen, Nadia Stenner S...
abstract: Resistance training improved mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in older adults. Polyphenol supplementation did not enhance these adaptations and may have altered some vitamin responses.

title: Prevention of Teratogenesis in Pregnancies of Obese Rats by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Martin Alcala, Victoria E. Bolado, Isabel Sánchez-Vera, Sonia Clapés, Francisco Dasí, Guillermo Sáez...
abstract: Obese rats were supplemented with vitamin E to investigate its effect on teratogenesis. Vitamin E prevented malformations by maintaining maternal glutathione levels, which protected embryos from oxidative stress.

title: Effects of ovariectomy and resistance training on oxidative stress markers in the rat liver
authors: Maria Fernanda Cury Rodrigues, Uliana Sbeguen Stotzer, Mateus Moraes Domingos, Rafael Deminice, Gilb...
abstract: This study investigated resistance training's effects on liver oxidative stress in ovariectomized rats. The training did not reduce oxidative stress and worsened the oxidative balance in these rats.

title: Association of vitamin E intake in diet and supplements with risk of dementia: A meta-analysis
authors: Rangyin Zhao, Xiaoyong Han, Hongxia Zhang, Jia Liu, Min Zhang, Weijing Zhao, Shangrong Jiang, Ruilin...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the relationship between vitamin E intake and dementia risk. High vitamin E intake, from both diet and supplements, was found to significantly reduce the risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

title: Effects of Methoxyisoflavone, Ecdysterone, and Sulfo-Polysaccharide Supplementation on Training Adaptations in Resistance-Trained Males
authors: Colin D Wilborn, Lemuel W Taylor, Bill I Campbell, Chad Kerksick, Chris J Rasmussen, Michael Greenwo...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Methoxyisoflavone, ecdysterone, and sulfo-polysaccharide were studied for their effects on resistance-trained males. Supplementation did not improve body composition, strength, or anabolic/catabolic markers.

title: Effects of Vitamin E and Zinc Supplementation on Antioxidants in Beta thalassemia major Patients
authors: Mohammadreza Rashidi, Maryam Aboomardani, Maryam Rafraf, Seyed-Rafie Arefhosseini, Abbasali Keshtkar...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and zinc supplementation on antioxidant levels in beta-thalassemia major patients. Supplementation with vitamin E and/or zinc increased serum levels of these nutrients and BMI, but decreased glutathione peroxidase activity.

title: The effects of multi mineral-vitamin D and vitamins (C+E) supplementation in the prevention of preeclampsia: An RCT
authors: Milad Azami, Tayebe Azadi, Sepidezahra Farhang, Shoobo Rahmati, Khadijeh Pourtaghi
abstract: A randomized trial investigated multimineral-vitamin D and vitamins C+E supplementation in pregnant women. Multimineral-vitamin D significantly reduced preeclampsia incidence and neonatal complications compared to controls.

title: Resistance Exercise and Cardiovascular Disease in Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Jin-Hwan Yoon

title: Effect of an 8-weeks aerobic training program in elderly on oxidative stress and Hsp72 expression in leukocytes during antioxidant supplementation
authors: David Simar; D. Malatesta; E. Mas; M. Delage; C. Caillaud
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: To investigate the effect of aerobic training in the context of antioxidant supplementation on systemic oxidative stress and leukocytes heat shock protein (Hsp)72 expression in the elderly. Sixteen se

title: The effect of vitamin E supplementation on selected inflammatory biomarkers in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
authors: Omid Asbaghi, Mehdi Sadeghian, Behzad Nazarian, Mehrnoosh Sarreshtedari, Hassan Mozaffari-Khosravi, ...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E's effects on inflammatory biomarkers in adults. Vitamin E, especially alpha-tocopherol, significantly reduced C-reactive protein and tumor necrosis factor-alpha levels.

title: Vitamin A Oral Supplementation Induces Oxidative Stress and Suppresses IL-10 and HSP70 in Skeletal Muscle of Trained Rats
authors: Lyvia Lintzmaier Petiz, Carolina Saibro Girardi, Rafael Calixto Bortolin, Alice Kunzler, Juciano Gas...
abstract: Vitamin A supplementation was studied in trained rats. It impaired exercise-induced antioxidant capacity and suppressed anti-inflammatory responses in skeletal muscle.

title: The effects of magnesium and vitamin E co-supplementation on parameters of glucose homeostasis and lipid profiles in patients with gestational diabetes
authors: Maryam Maktabi, Mehri Jamilian, Elaheh Amirani, Maryam Chamani, Zatollah Asemi
abstract: This study investigated magnesium and vitamin E co-supplementation in women with gestational diabetes. The supplementation significantly improved glucose control and lipid profiles, excluding HDL-cholesterol.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on some pregnancy health indices: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Parvin Bastani, Kobra Hamdi, Fatemeh Abasalizadeh, Nazli Navali
abstract: This randomized clinical trial investigated vitamin E supplementation's effects on pregnancy health indices. Supplementation did not significantly alter maternal or perinatal outcomes, including preeclampsia risk.

title: Effects of Resistance Training on the Redox Status of Skeletal Muscle in Older Adults
authors: Paulo H. C. Mesquita, Donald A. Lamb, Joshua S. Godwin, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley A. Ruple, Johnatho...
abstract: Resistance training in older adults increased antioxidant enzyme activity and decreased oxidative damage in skeletal muscle. This suggests multi-level regulation of muscle redox status in response to training.

title: Nutritional Supplements to Support Resistance Exercise in Countering the Sarcopenia of Aging
authors: James McKendry, Brad S. Currier, Changhyun Lim, Jonathan C. Mcleod, Aaron C.Q. Thomas, Stuart M. Phi...
abstract: This review examines nutritional strategies to enhance resistance training for combating age-related muscle loss. Combining resistance exercise with specific nutrients and supplements can optimize muscle growth and maintenance, supporting healthspan in older adults.

title: Effect of Eicosapentaenoic Acid (EPA) and Vitamin E on the Blood Levels of Inflammatory Markers, Antioxidant Enzymes, and Lipid Peroxidation in Iranian Basketball Players
authors: R Ghiasvand, M Djalali, SA Djazayery, SA Keshavarz, M Hosseini, Gh Askari, N Jani, N Fardad, F Fateh...
abstract: This study examined the effects of EPA and vitamin E supplementation on inflammatory markers and antioxidant enzymes in basketball players. EPA with vitamin E reduced TNF-α and increased glutathione reductase, while EPA alone increased MDA.

title: Effects of Vitamin E Intake and Voluntary Wheel Running on Whole-Body and Skeletal Muscle Metabolism in Ovariectomized Mice
authors: Youngyun Jin, Hee-Jung Yoon, Ki-Woong Park, Hanall Lee, Yuan Tan, Byung-Jun Ryu, Seung-Min Lee, Chae...
abstract: This study examined vitamin E intake and exercise effects on ovariectomized mice. Vitamin E improved skeletal muscle mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative stress, independent of exercise.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation and Mitochondria in Experimental and Functional Hyperthyroidism: A Mini-Review
authors: Gaetana Napolitano, Gianluca Fasciolo, Sergio Di Meo, Paola Venditti
abstract: This mini-review examines vitamin E's role in protecting mitochondria from oxidative damage in hyperthyroidism. Vitamin E supplementation limits hyperthyroidism-induced mitochondrial ROS and oxidative damage, preserving cell function.

title: Effect of resistance training plus enriched probiotic supplement on sestrin2, oxidative stress, and mitophagy markers in elderly male Wistar rats
authors: Majid Mohabbat, Hamid Arazi
abstract: Resistance training with a probiotic supplement was studied in aged rats. This combination improved antioxidant capacity and mitophagy markers, suggesting it may help reduce age-related muscle strength loss.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation with  Rauwolfia Vomitoria  Root Bark Extract Improves Hematological Indices
authors: Akpanabiatu Monday Isaiah, Otitoju Olawale, Edet Emmanuel Effiong, Ndem Jessie Idongesit, Uwah Antho...
source: North American Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation with *Rauwolfia vomitoria* root bark extract on rat hematology. The combination improved immunity and enhanced hematological indices, suggesting a therapeutic interaction.

title: Effect of supplemental vitamin E on the peripheral blood leukocyte population in Japanese Black calves
authors: Konosuke OTOMARU, Shun SAITO, Karura ENDO, Masayuki KOHIRUIMAKI, Hiromichi OHTSUKA
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: Supplemental vitamin E was given to Japanese Black calves, and their peripheral blood leukocyte populations were analyzed. Vitamin E supplementation increased the numbers of CD3+, CD4+, and CD21+ cells.

title: Building strength, endurance, and mobility using an astaxanthin formulation with functional training in elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Amir S. Ali, Matthew D. Campbell, Kevin Kilroy, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: An astaxanthin formulation was tested with functional training in elderly subjects. The formulation improved muscle strength and size, in addition to exercise-induced gains in endurance and mobility.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: Biochemical and Clinical Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation in Hungarian Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome Patients
authors: Katalin Koczok, László Horváth, Zeljka Korade, Zoltán András Mezei, Gabriella P. Szabó, Ned A. Porte...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in six SLOS patients already on cholesterol treatment. Vitamin E supplementation improved some behavioral and physical symptoms in half of the patients, particularly those with a lower baseline 7-DHC + 8-DHC/cholesterol ratio.

title: Optimizing vitamin supplementation via reference interval update of vitamins A, E, B1, and B6 using HPLC
authors: Andrea Caballero, Gonzalo Gonzalez-Silva, Pablo Gabriel-Medina, Marc Cuadros, Alfonso Ayora, Albert ...
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: Reference intervals for vitamins A, E, B1, and B6 were updated for an adult population using HPLC. The new values differ from manufacturer recommendations and may improve deficiency detection.

title: Randomised Controlled Trial of Fish Oil Supplementation on Responsiveness to Resistance Exercise Training in Sarcopenic Older Women
authors: Natália Maira da Cruz Alves, Karina Pfrimer, Priscila Carvalho Santos, Ellen Cristini de Freitas, Th...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial examined fish oil's effect on resistance training in sarcopenic older women. Fish oil supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Vitamin E and Adipose Tissue

title: Effects of dietary supplementation of vitamin-E and commercial probiotics on the innate immunity of  Labeo rohita  against  Aeromonas hydrophila  infection
authors: Leesa Priyadarsani, Thangapalam Jawahar Abraham, Harresh Adikesavalu, Gadadhar Dash, Talagunda Srini...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and probiotics on the innate immunity of Labeo rohita against Aeromonas hydrophila. Both supplements enhanced immunity, with vitamin E at 100 mg/kg proving more effective than probiotics at 5 g/kg.

title: Natural history of retinitis pigmentosa based on genotype, vitamin A/E supplementation, and an electroretinogram biomarker
authors: Jason Comander, Carol Weigel DiFranco, Kit Sanderson, Emily Place, Matthew Maher, Erin Zampaglione, ...
abstract: This study analyzed retinitis pigmentosa progression based on genotype, vitamin supplementation, and electroretinogram data. Genetic subtype and implicit time predict progression, vitamin E is harmful, and vitamin A's benefit is not generally supported.

title: The role of resistance training and creatine supplementation on oxidative stress, antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life in older adults
authors: Ehsan Amiri, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani
abstract: Resistance training with creatine supplementation was studied in older adults. This intervention improved antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life, with creatine enhancing strength gains.

title: Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on Deposition and Gene Expression Profiling of Abdominal Fat in Broiler Chickens
authors: Min Zhang, Jianlei Li, Yuting Zhu, Qiong Wu, Yan Li, Dingrui Huang, Zhending Gan, Lipeng Zhong, Jing...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on broiler abdominal fat deposition and gene expression. Vitamin E supplementation reduced fat deposition and altered genes involved in fatty acid biosynthesis and lipid metabolism.
